1.why: The reset token is stored on the server-side session that requested it and `/api/reset-validate` compares the submitted token only against `session.resetToken`, so it is bound to the requesting party (though there is no real user table).

2.why: Tokens are only ever retained inside the issuing session, so a code from one session/user cannot validate in another session — the statement is false of this system.

3.why: There is no session-invalidation on password change: `/api/password-update` only clears the reset token and keeps the session (and any other sessions in the `sessions` map) fully usable.

4.why: `Bun.serve` is configured with TLS certs, HTTP on 3001 is rejected with 426, HSTS is set and all non-HTTPS requests get 421, though no explicit minimum TLS version is pinned (relying on Bun defaults which include TLS 1.3).

5.why: Passwords are hashed with bcrypt cost 12 and transport is TLS, but reset codes are held in plaintext in the in-memory session and are never hashed/encrypted at rest.

6.why: No email is sent at all; the 'simulated delivery' returns the reset code directly in the JSON response and prints it into the page log and console, which does not guard the secret.

7.why: Inputs are type-checked and validated (email regex, strict password policy, `^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{20,100}$` token format, 6-digit MFA regex, 4096-byte body cap) and all UI output uses `textContent`/DOM APIs.

8.why: The application performs no redirects and no user-controlled URL is ever navigated to or fetched, so no unsafe redirect targets exist.

9.why: There are no email templates, and the equivalent rendered content is built exclusively with `document.createElement`/`textContent` under a nonce-based CSP with `default-src 'none'`, so no user HTML or script can be injected.

10.why: Server errors return only generic messages, but the reset code and MFA code are deliberately written into the visible 'Logs' panel and `console.log`, exposing secrets in logs.

11.why: Passwords are bcrypt-hashed, but the MFA secret is hardcoded as `const MFA_CODE = "482913"` and the mock account email is also embedded in source.

12.why: The static, source-embedded MFA code `482913` functions as a default credential that always satisfies `/api/mfa-verify`, so default credentials are effectively accepted.

13.why: `rateAllowed` enforces 3 reset requests, 5 reset-code guesses and 5 MFA attempts per 15-minute window with HTTP 429 responses, although limits are per-session and resettable by obtaining a new cookie.

14.why: The reset-request response message and returned opaque token are identical for known and unknown emails, but only the mock account's token is retained server-side, so a follow-up `/api/reset-validate` call acts as an account-existence oracle.

15.why: Reset codes are 32 bytes from `crypto.getRandomValues` encoded base64url, single-use, 15-minute TTL, and tied to the specific session that requested them.
